entities.name: Abelardo Alvarado Alcántara
entities.label: Person
entities.summary:
Abelardo Alvarado Alcántara (1919–2009) was a Mexican Catholic bishop who served as auxiliary bishop of Guadalajara for three decades, becoming one of the most durable pastoral figures in western Mexico's largest diocese. Born in Jalisco, he was ordained a priest in 1944 and rose through parish ministry before his episcopal consecration in 1966.

During his long service under three successive archbishops of Guadalajara, Alvarado Alcántara contributed to diocesan administration, seminary formation, and social outreach programmes in a region historically marked by intense Catholic identity and the memory of the Cristero War. He participated in the post-conciliar pastoral renewal called for by Vatican II, helping to adapt parish structures and catechetical methods to urban growth in the Guadalajara metropolitan area.

Although not a figure of international prominence, Alvarado Alcántara exemplified the steady institutional work of auxiliary bishops who translate conciliar vision into local pastoral reality. His longevity in office meant that generations of Guadalajaran clergy and laity were shaped by his priestly example. He retired in 1995 and died in 2009, remembered as a faithful servant of one of Mexico's most historically significant archdioceses.

entities.summary: Abelardo Alvarado Alcántara was a Mexican Roman Catholic prelate who served as the auxiliary bishop of the Roman Catholic Archdiocese of Mexico City from 1985 until 2008. He was also the Secretary General of the Episcopal Conference of Mexico (CEM) from 1997 to 2004.
